column2: Armathaim Sipha, Elkanah, Jerahmeel, Elihu, Thoke and in Nasib Ephraim retain the selected genealogy and geographical expressions.
column3: The relation of Nasib Ephraim to the genealogy is not independently resolved; no familiar Zuph genealogy is silently substituted.

column2: Two wives are named Hannah and Peninnah, with children for Peninnah and no child for Hannah; the singular/plural contrast remains.
Year by year renders the recurring-days idiom; the journey from Armathaim is for worship and sacrifice at Shiloh to the Lord God Sabaoth, with Eli and both priestly sons present.
Elkanah's sacrifice is followed by portions for Peninnah, her sons and daughters; the full beneficiary list remains.
Hannah receives one portion because she has no child, though Elkanah loves her more than the other woman; the Lord closes her womb.
column3: This other woman identifies the contextual referent of tauten as Peninnah. The womb wording compresses the things-about-the-womb expression, not a different physical claim.

column2: The repeated childlessness, affliction and despondency remain, with the Lord's shutting the womb stated as the reason and no-child outcome.
column3: In her affliction renders the selected kata phrases contextually; the exact relation of those phrases to the withholding of a child remains open.

column2: The annual action and Hannah's repeated ascent, despondency, weeping and refusal of food remain.
column3: He would do this supplies the contextual subject of the unexpressed poiei; the precise backward reference of this remains a narrative question.

column2: Elkanah calls Hannah, she answers Here I am, and he asks three questions before comparing himself with ten children; the striking-heart image remains.
column3: My lord is ordinary human address to her husband, not divine Thou; children preserves tekna rather than narrowing to sons.

column2: After they eat at Shiloh, Hannah rises and stands before the Lord while Eli sits by the sanctuary doorposts; the selected standing notice remains.
Anguish of soul leads to prayer and emphatic weeping; abundantly renders the repeated weeping construction.
The vow retains Adonai, Lord, Eloai Sabaoth, emphatic looking, remembrance, male offspring and lifelong gift, with no wine/intoxicant and no iron on the head.
column3: Thou, Thy and Thee are direct singular divine address. Iron is not narrowed to razor, and an unexpressed Nazirite label is not added.

column2: Her prolonged prayer precedes Eli's watching her mouth; continued conveys the multiplying-prayer construction.
Speech in her heart, moving lips and an unheard voice lead to Eli's mistaken drunkenness assessment; the narrator does not endorse that assessment.
Eli's servant, not Eli, asks about drunkenness and commands removal of wine and departure from the Lord's presence; the selected speaker remains.
Hannah denies drinking wine or intoxicant, describes her hard day and says she pours out her soul before the Lord; ordinary my lord remains human address.
She asks not to be classed as a pestilent daughter and explains her prolonged speech from abundant murmuring.
column3: Pestilent daughter and murmuring for loime/ adoleschia remain provisional lexical choices; no daughter-of-Belial or grief-only wording is silently substituted.

column2: Propose grant you the whole request to make the Greek soi recipient explicit in Eli's blessing; the request already made of God remains unchanged.
Hannah says her handmaid has found favour, then enters her lodging, eats with her husband, drinks and no longer has a fallen face.
column3: Has found retains the selected assertion rather than converting it to a wish; fallen face is the source's countenance image.

column2: Early rising, worship and departure lead to Elkanah's return to Armathaim, knowing Hannah and the Lord's remembrance; the sentence continues with conception in verse 20.
column3: Past English narrates the initial Greek historical presents without claiming a change in event sequence; knew preserves the sexual idiom.

column2: Conception opens this stored unit, then birth and Samuel's naming are linked to asking him of the Lord God Sabaoth; the selected divine title remains.
Elkanah and all his household go up for the yearly sacrifice, his vows and all land tithes; the three offering categories remain.
column3: Vow offerings interprets vows in the sacrificial context; Shiloh renders the selected Silom form without asserting a different destination.

column2: Hannah delays ascent until the child's weaning and appearance before the Lord, where he will remain for ever.
column3: Not until supplies the negative from the narrator's did-not-go context for her elliptical speech; the selected conditional/temporal weaning construction remains provisional.

column2: Elkanah approves what is good in her eyes, tells her to stay until weaning and asks the Lord to establish what came from her mouth; the selected your is not changed to His.
A three-year-old calf, loaves, an oiphi of fine flour and a nebel of wine accompany ascent to Shiloh and the Lord's house, with the child present.
column3: The calf is singular with an age designation, not three bulls. Oiphi and nebel retain source-grounded quantity/container terms without invented modern equivalences.

column2: They bring him before the Lord; his father slaughters the annual sacrifice, brings the child and slaughters the calf, then Hannah brings him to Eli.
column3: The extended selected sequence is retained even where actions appear repeated; him as the first object's identity and Hannah's later object are contextual English supplies.

column2: Hannah's respectful petition and as-your-soul-lives oath identify her as the woman who stood before Eli praying to the Lord; ordinary you remains.
For this child recalls the prayer, followed by the Lord's giving her the request she asked; the repeated request language remains.
She lends him to the Lord for every day he lives, as a loan to the Lord; both lending and loan terms are preserved without replacing them by a generic dedication.
